s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic swelling and discharge of the right upper eyelid with underlying sinus involvement
salient_findings: 2-year history of swelling of the right upper eyelid
Discharge of pus for the previous 10 months
Immovable scarlike node on the right upper eyelid
Opacification and expansion of the right frontal, ethmoid, and maxillary sinuses
key_facts: 52-year-old Japanese woman
2-year history of swelling of the right upper eyelid
Discharge of pus for the previous 10 months
No trauma to the head
No symptoms such as fever, headache, or nasal discharge
Immovable scarlike node on the right upper eyelid
Node size: 11 × 7 mm
MRI findings: high signal on T2-weighted image and ring enhancement in the right frontal sinus
CT findings: opacification and expansion of the right frontal, ethmoid, and maxillary sinuses
No bone destruction
Histopathology: mild inflammatory infiltrate with fibrosis, lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate, few eosinophils, and no sign of malignancy

s4.champion: Chronic frontal sinusitis with cutaneous fistula

raw.champion: Chronic frontal sinusitis with cutaneous fistula
raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms, including a 2-year history of swelling of the right upper eyelid and discharge of pus for 10 months, along with imaging studies showing opacification and expansion of the right frontal sinus without bone destruction, and histopathology revealing mild inflammatory infiltrate, are most consistent with chronic frontal sinusitis complicated by a cutaneous fistula.

rejected.label: Pott's puffy tumor with sinocutaneous fistula
rejected.why: Pott's puffy tumor typically presents with more severe symptoms such as fever and headache due to its association with intracranial complications, which are not present in this case.

rejected.label: Chronic sinusitis with mucocele and cutaneous fistula
rejected.why: While possible, the specific involvement of the frontal sinus and the absence of mention of a mucocele in imaging studies make this less likely compared to chronic frontal sinusitis with a cutaneous fistula.

rejected.label: Frontal sinus mucocele
rejected.why: A mucocele would typically present with expansion and erosion of the sinus walls, which is not indicated by the CT findings showing no bone destruction.

rejected.label: Subperiosteal abscess of the frontal bone
rejected.why: The presence of a chronic discharge and a fistula, along with the specific sinus involvement, points more towards a chronic sinusitis complication rather than an isolated subperiosteal abscess.
